records.public_safe_text: unit 1 was stopped at red light at [roadway]. unit 2, a pedestrian, was standing in the northeast corner waiting for the pedestrian signal light to turn. unit 1 proceeded to turn north, and at the same time, unit 2 proceeded [roadway] to cross in the crosswalk. unit 1 collided with unit 2, causing unit 1's tires go over unit 2's feet. the investigating officer was not able to determine the contributing factor due to both units stating two opposite stories. unit 1 driver stated his light turned green, and the pedestrian sign was red palm. unit 2 stated the pedestrian signal was counting down, and as he stepped into the crosswalk, unit 1 collided with him. the investigating officer observed when the pedestrian button is not pushed, the pedestrian sign will stay red when westbound traffic has a green light. however, when the pedestrian button is pushed, the walk signal turns to a green man and counts down from 33 while at the same time the westbound traffic light is green. the crash scene and all interviews were recorded on a body-worn camera. the video and/or photographs were saved to evidence. com on id#24-0669201.

records.deidentified_narrative: police responded to the listed incident in reference to a accident private property. i arrived on scene and spoke to the driver of u1. u1 driver advised that her vehicle slipped out of park and into reverse while she was sitting in the driver seat. u1 driver advised she may have touched the gas but just kept repeating that ""it slipped"". i then spoke to u2 owner, who was not occupying the vehicle at the time of incident. u2 owner had surveillance video of u1 reversing at a high rate of speed and striking her vehicle, sending u2 over the parking curb and onto the grass, into the apartment #1505 causing intrusion of about 8"". i then spoke to ofc. montalbo #890 who had spoke to pedestrian. pedestrian advised ofc. montalbo that he was laying in bed when he heard the vehicle crash into his apartment, his bed is propped against the wall that u2 struck. pedestrian advised that he felt the bed shake and when he moved his neck immediately hurt. pedestrian was transported to mission trails baptist due to the injury by medic 22. all involved parties were provided case cards and advised of report being written. it should be noted that driver of u1, interviewed approximately 2 hours after incident, had not been supervised entirely while waiting for officers, appeared to be intoxicated. u1 driver was struggling with comprehension, repeating herself, slurring speech, had bloodshot watery eyes, and an odor of intoxicants emitting from her person. due to the extreme time lapse and the fact that she had returned inside her apartment unsupervised, i was unable to determine if u1 driver had consumed alcohol since the accident. however, when offered the opportunity to conduct sfsts to disprove any intoxication, u1 driver refused. i then returned to service, digital media evidence is available.

observed gina holmes (black female, date of birth: [date], contact number: [phone]) standing near william parker (white male, date of birth:[date]) who was laying on the shoulder on [roadway]. parker will be labeled at unit two for this crash report. i also observed a white ford explorer bearing texas registration [identifier] parked between the entrance ramp to interstate 30 [roadway]. this vehicle will be labeled as unit one in this crash report. i made contact with holmes [roadway]. holmes stated she had been [roadway] when she observed parker standing in the roadway. holmes stated she called 911 to report parker being in the roadway. holmes stated parker was wearing dark clothing and she was startled by his presence in the roadway and swerved in order to avoid hitting parker with her vehicle. holmes stated she proceeded to circle around and came back to offer parker assistance. holmes stated when she arrived back at the location where she had observed parker, she parked her vehicle and attempted to speak to parker. holmes stated parker was standing in the middle of the entrance ramp to interstate 30 west. holmes stated parker seemed to be confused and did not respond to her. holmes stated as she was trying to assist parker when a white suv struck parker. cpl lamont made contact with the james rainer (white male, date of birth: [date], contact number: [phone]) who was the driver of the ford explorer which struck parker. during the investigation rainer stated he did not see parker in the roadway due to the lack of light on the roadway and parker's dark clothing. rainer stated he heard and felt the impact when he struck parker however was unaware, he had struck a pedestrian until he spoke to holmes. due to the evidence, i observed at the scene and the witness statements provided by the witnesses, i determined parker was the at fault party

records.deidentified_narrative: police responded to a report of a crash in which a pedestrian was hit by a motor vehicle on the property of a wal-mart. when i arrived i found that the pedestrian was on the ground with her legs still partially underneath unit. the driver of unit 1 had previously been detained by an off duty bexar county sherriff's officer who was working at the location, and there were multiple bystanders in the area. i spoke with one female briefly who stated that she saw the incident. she described seeing the pedestrian walking through the lot from a side door of the store. unit 1 drove towards her and hit her. she confirmed that she saw the driver driving the vehicle and saw him exit the vehicle from the driver seat. the driver of unit 1 confirmed that the vehicle belonged to him and that he was driving the vehicle. he was not able to tell me how the accident happened, only stated that his steering wheel was not working properly. i asked if he applied the brake. he stated he did apply the brake but that the brakes had some issues also. safd ems transported the pedestrian to sammc for her injuries. updated injury status for unit 1 driver and unit 2. [identifier]

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1, a bob-tailed tractor truck, was traveling eb on ih10 near the 523mp in heavy fog (approximate sight distance was 250-300ft). unit 1 came upon a crash that had just occurred on the right side of the roadway used faulty evasive actions and attempted to avoid the debris field by braking and merging into the center median where pedestrians and other vehicles had parked in order to help with the previous crashes, and even though the main lanes were clear of vehicles and only light debris was in the roadway. unit 1 struck the cable barrier with the left distributed and then a pedestrian that had stopped to assist with the first collision. the pedestrian, who was noted to have been wearing black pants and long sleeve hoodie, was struck with the front left of unit 1 and then fell under the truck. unit 1 continued back onto the roadway and came to a stop on the right side. the pedestrian came to rest in the cable barrier and was pronounced deceased by kendall county justice of the peace f. pressler. unit 1 driver stated that he knew the truck would take longer to stop due to it being bob-tailed. unit 1 was inspected post crash and was placed out of service for diminished braking efficiency that was determined to have been present before the crash. no damage was done to the braking system during or after the crash. unit 1 was found to have only 77% braking efficiency (f=. 34) and was traveling at approximately 76mph (111. 42 ft/sec) this gives the vehicle a braking to stop distance of 566'. if unit 1 did not have a braking issue then the stopping distance with 100% braking (f=. 44) would have been 437'. further showing that the vehicle was traveling too fast for the conditions of the vehicle and weather.
